tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description starts with imperative phrasing 'Use this skill when an EC2 patch run has failed...', focuses on user-facing triggers (failed/timed-out/cancelled patch runs, non-compliance, specific error types), explicitly lists many trigger contexts including edge cases like 'even when the cause looks obvious or the user only pastes an error message', and remains a concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an EC2 patch run has failed, or a user asks why patching failed or how to fix it, and load it first even when the cause looks obvious or the user only pastes an error message or code.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but entirely domain-specific — it describes AWS SSM/EC2 patch failure diagnosis procedures, gates, and SOP selection logic. It does not explain general concepts the agent already knows (e.g., what EC2 or SSM is); every sentence conveys project-specific conventions, exact parameter names, and non-obvious gate rules.
tests.evidence: 'SSM always takes a lock to stop parallel runs. A lock message is almost never the cause; look past it to the real failure.'

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large reference tables (API docs, error code tables, long threshold lists) are embedded in the body. Tables present (parameter notes, plugin names, step-selection rules) are short and operational, not bulk reference data; detailed SOP content lives in references/sops/.
tests.evidence: Table of document parameters and plugin names are short (6-7 rows) and directly instructional, not large reference dumps.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file listed under references/ (sop-index.md, execution-guide.md, remediation-plan-template.md, command-plan-template.md, and each sop-*.md file) has a markdown link in the body using the references/ path format.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The Files table explicitly states the step number and condition for loading each reference file (e.g., 'Step 6, first', 'Steps 10 and 12').
tests.evidence: '[references/sop-index.md](references/sop-index.md) | Step 6, first: find candidate SOPs by category, platform and symptoms.'

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All references/ links use relative paths from the skill root with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (running commands, re-patching, gate checks) are highly prescriptive with exact rules ('never edit inside a code block', 'one step per send_command'), while root-cause diagnosis and SOP matching leave room for judgment with explained rationale ('look past it to the real failure'). This matches specificity to fragility well.
tests.evidence: 'Never run a command that isn't in an SOP, never change an SOP command' vs. 'Read the whole error output and identify the exact failure.'

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present competing tool alternatives for the same task without a default; it uses deterministic lookup (SOP index) rather than open tool choice, so the 'menu' pattern doesn't really apply here.
tests.evidence: No multiple-tool-choice language is present; the skill does not apply to this test's typical case.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (identify instance, check gates, find root cause, select SOP, select applicable steps, execute, re-patch) that applies across any patch failure instance, not a one-off declarative task.
tests.evidence: 'Copy this checklist and work through it in order. Steps 1-8 run in every mode...'

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A 'Common pitfalls' section is present with concrete, non-obvious corrections specific to this domain (e.g., treating lock messages as the cause, editing SOP commands to fit).
tests.evidence: 'Treating "lock" as the cause | SSM always takes a lock. Find the real failure.'

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly provides output templates (remediation-plan-template.md and command-plan-template.md) referenced for the required structured output.
tests.evidence: '[references/remediation-plan-template.md](references/remediation-plan-template.md) | Step 8: the format of the Remediation plan.'

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline template is embedded in the body; the plan/command-plan formats are stored in references/ and only the required output line list is given inline, which is short.
tests.evidence: 'Every answer about a patch failure... must contain these lines, in this order: Root cause:, SOP:... Status:.'

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file devops-agent-patch-elevated-role.yaml is linked in the Files table.
tests.evidence: '[assets/devops-agent-patch-elevated-role.yaml](assets/devops-agent-patch-elevated-role.yaml) | Only when a directed action is refused because the account has no elevated role...'

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies the exact condition for when to point the operator to it.
tests.evidence: 'Only when a directed action is refused because the account has no elevated role: point the operator to this CloudFormation template. Don't deploy it yourself.'

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from skill root with no traversal or absolute path.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural workflow uses checkbox checklist format with 'Step N:' naming, and detailed sections below reference the same step numbers (e.g., '### Step 1: Identify the instance...').
tests.evidence: '- [ ] Step 1: Identify the instance and the failed `AWS-RunPatchBaseline` run' ... '### Step 1: Identify the instance and the failed run'

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation step before presenting the plan, checking for verbatim commands, no placeholders, and format matching.
tests.evidence: 'Before presenting the plan, check it: every command block is copied verbatim from the chosen SOP, no `<...>` placeholder is left, and every value copied from the failed run matches its format.'
